title: Atlas incident postmortem: change stream lag
summary: Postmortem for the October 28 Sev1: the billing change stream consumer fell 19 hours behind after a deploy and nearly ran past the 26-hour oplog window (K-02). Locked D-14: the consumer checkpoints its resume token in Atlas every 1,000 events and pages on-call when lag exceeds 5 minutes, and T-01: Marcus adds the lag alert and a resync runbook before launch.
utterances: Postmortem for Tuesday's Sev1. Marcus, timeline please.
Monday 14:00 we deployed the billing consumer. It crashed in a loop on one malformed event and nobody noticed.
Tuesday 09:00 finance saw invoices frozen. By then the change stream was 19 hours behind.
And the oplog window at peak is about 26 hours. We were seven hours from losing the resume token.
That's K-02. Which means a full resync of usage, during launch prep.
We alert on consumer process down, not on lag. The process was up, just restarting.
So alert on lag directly. Compare the last processed event time with now.
And checkpoint the resume token in Atlas every thousand events, so a restart picks up where it left off instead of replaying from memory.
Proposal: checkpoint every 1,000 events, page on-call when lag passes five minutes.
Five minutes is tight but billing can tolerate it. Agreed.
Marcus, can you own the alert plus a resync runbook before launch?
Yes, I'll have both done by November 14.
Also the malformed event goes to a dead letter collection instead of crashing the loop.
Good, I'll fold that into the same change.

locks.text: The billing change stream consumer checkpoints its resume token in Atlas every 1,000 events, sends malformed events to a dead-letter collection, and pages on-call when lag exceeds 5 minutes.
Marcus adds the change stream lag alert and a resync runbook before the public API launch (due November 14).
